elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause states that Licensor may request an audit “no more than once in any 12-month period.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 30 days’ advance notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “at least 30 days’ prior” notice.

elements.element: Audit notice must be in writing.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires “prior written notice.”

elements.element: Audits must be conducted during Customer’s business hours.
elements.evidence: Each audit must be conducted during “Licensee’s normal business hours.”
The clause requires an “independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional.”

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires an auditor “bound by confidentiality obligations.”

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit cost by default.
elements.evidence: The cost provision states that the audit cost will be borne by Licensor.

elements.element: Customer may be required to bear the audit cost only if the audit identifies an underpayment exceeding 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs upon discovery of any “discrepancy” exceeding 5%, rather than only an underpayment exceeding 5%. Because this governs future audits, the underpayment condition is not demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Vendor must have no direct access to Customer’s systems.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that “Licensor shall have no direct access to Licensee’s systems.”

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The restriction to no more than once in any 12-month period is at least as protective as once per year.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 15 days’ advance notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days’ prior notice, which exceeds the 15-day fallback requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit cost by default.
elements.evidence: The cost provision states that the audit cost will be borne by Licensor.

elements.element: Customer may be required to bear the audit cost only if the audit identifies an underpayment exceeding 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs for any “discrepancy” exceeding 5%; it neither limits the trigger to an underpayment nor preserves Vendor responsibility through the 10% threshold.

result.reason: Neither position is fully satisfied because the cost-shifting trigger remains a broadly defined discrepancy above 5%, rather than an underpayment above the applicable 5% preferred or 10% fallback threshold. The redline is also not minimal because it adds an off-site-wherever-possible restriction that neither position requires, and it awkwardly places the audit-cost paragraph before the audit provision to which it refers. Unrelated commercial terms are not contradicted.
